clue.text: Attempt to secure one pound for hat

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so the attempt wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: an attempt is a try
one is the Roman numeral I
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone tries to pay a pound to get hold of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown, so it is one example of headwear.

clue.text: Follows page in state of panic

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A page boy follows someone and ends up panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is a spiralling dive of an aircraft, used figuratively for a state of panic or chaos.

clue.text: Urge simple changes around university

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
changes means alters, so the letters of simple are rearranged

explanation.surface: Campaigners urge simple reforms across the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SIMPLE into IMPLSE, which then goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge to act, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Advocate roadblock across street

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the roadblock word straddles the street abbreviation

parts.note: a roadblock is a barrier

explanation.surface: A campaigner sets up a roadblock across the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who pleads in court, which is what an advocate does.

clue.text: Respectable poker hand

definitions.meaning: conventional and honest, not criminal or deviant
five cards in sequence, a ranked combination in poker

explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest and conventional in slang, and in poker it names a run of five consecutive cards.

clue.text: Here's the very person to speak, about Satan

parts.note: to speak means to talk
of means about, as in a story of something
Satan is the Devil

explanation.surface: Introducing just the person to lecture on the subject of Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when someone arrives just as they are being discussed, as if to say here is the very person.

clue.text: Superior, British in flying boat

indicators.note: in puts the British letter inside the rearranged letters
flying suggests the letters scatter, so boat is rearranged

explanation.surface: A British pilot is seen in a flying boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges BOAT into ABOT, and B goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a religious house is called its superior, and an abbot heads a monastery.

clue.text: Brave social worker following humiliation

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the worker comes after the humiliation

parts.note: gall can mean vexation or a sore humiliation
ants are social insects, and the workers do the labour

explanation.surface: A social worker shows courage after being humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a profession, but it is an ANT, a worker in a social insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means courageous and heroic, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: Hear about wolf down in Deal?

indicators.note: about means around, so the hearing word encloses the eating word

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
to wolf down food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Hearing about someone bolting food down in the town of Deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a Kent town, but here it means an agreement; the question mark marks the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, so it is a kind of deal.

clue.text: Where one may order round after round

definitions.text: Where one may order round after round

parts.words: Where one may order round after round
parts.note: after a round of golf, players go to the clubhouse bar to buy rounds of drinks

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call the clubhouse bar the extra hole after the eighteenth, where drinks follow the game.

clue.text: Just one militant seizing power?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the militant word closes round the next piece

parts.note: militant can mean warlike, which is martial
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A question whether a lone extremist could justly take control.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in the sense of fair and even-handed is a synonym, treating every side without favour.

clue.text: Rubbish can be left in large crate on the right

indicators.note: in places the left abbreviation within the word for large

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: the right-hand end of the word crate supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A tip about rubbish: it can go in a large crate to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for nonsense or worthless talk, a familiar synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Anger shown by sailor getting cross

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A sailor shows his temper by becoming irate.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal cross, as on the Scottish flag, so it is a type of cross.

clue.text: Derelict not in shed

parts.note: not in means out
to shed skin is to cast it

explanation.surface: An abandoned figure is found not inside the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict, as a noun, is a vagrant or person rejected by society, which is an outcast.

clue.text: Cack-handed at home, the last to use drill

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word the

parts.note: PT, physical training, is military-style drill exercise

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy at home is the last person to use a power drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' suggests a power tool, but it means PT, physical training. Cack-handed is British slang for clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cack-handed is British slang for clumsy, and inept means lacking skill or awkward.

clue.text: Guess tie's sorted, game over!

indicators.note: sorted means put in order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: checkmate, or mate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A chess player guesses the tie is settled and the game finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough guess at a value, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: End up engaging superb tutor in republic

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the reversed goal word holds the other pieces
up in a down clue means the word is read backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
ace means superb
a don is a university tutor

explanation.surface: Getting an excellent tutor finally in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End up' reads like a phrase, but End is AIM and 'up' turns it to MIA, which holds ACE and DON.
explanation.definitionFit: North Macedonia, once known simply by the shorter name, is a Balkan republic.

clue.text: Friend ringing a seabird is taking protective interest

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the friend word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A friend banding a seabird for study shows a protective interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests bird ringing, but it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternal means fatherly, as in caring for someone in a protective way.

clue.text: Cold cleaner changing carriage

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner moves from a cold carriage on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, named after the Duke of Clarence.

clue.text: In US, measure a length without distortion

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a measure of volume

explanation.surface: Americans measure a length exactly, without distortion.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal translation follows the original word for word, free of exaggeration or distortion.

clue.text: Conspirator caught in Jose's house?

indicators.note: in puts the cricket letter inside the Spanish house

parts.note: casa is Spanish for house, and Jose is a Spanish name
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A plotter is arrested at the home of someone called Jose.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the plotters who stabbed Julius Caesar, so he is a conspirator.

clue.text: Attacking player in match?

parts.note: reads as a forward in a football match, but also the part that strikes a match into flame

explanation.definitionFit: A forward who scores goals is called by this name, and a match is also a thing that is struck.

clue.text: Short battle for sausage

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the battle name loses its final letter

parts.note: Salamis was a sea battle where the Greeks beat the Persians in 480 BC

explanation.surface: A brief fight over a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spiced, cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Popped into a church in ancient city

indicators.note: popped suggests something burst apart, so the letters of into are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone nipped into a church while visiting an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popped' looks like a verb of movement with 'into', but it scrambles the word into, giving NTIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a great city of the ancient world, in what is now southern Turkey.

clue.text: Strange look upset Welsh girl

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: new can mean strange or unfamiliar
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An odd look upsets a girl from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NEWLO round to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Olwen is a Welsh female name, from the heroine of the tale Culhwch and Olwen.

clue.text: Back the animal that comes in last, commonly?

indicators.note: in common, Cockney speech the H is dropped from horse

parts.words: the animal that comes in last
parts.note: the horse that finishes at the end of a race, an end horse

explanation.surface: A punter asks whether to bet on the horse that finishes last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests betting, which fits the surface, but it is the definition. 'Commonly' signals Cockney pronunciation, dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or plan is to support it, and to endorse means to give approval or support.

clue.text: A quarrel about right marker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the quarrel word goes round the right letter

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A dispute arises over a correct marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' also means a crossbow bolt, tempting as the definition, but here it is ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign or symbol pointing the way, so it serves as a marker.

clue.text: Bulbs kept initially in paper

parts.note: onions are bulbs

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of kept is taken

explanation.surface: Bulbs are stored wrapped in paper at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is a thin, glossy, translucent writing paper, so it is a type of paper.

clue.text: I blacken the name of a Corsican, perhaps

parts.note: to slander someone is to blacken their name

explanation.surface: A confession of defaming a man from Corsica.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corsican lives on an island, so he is one example of an island dweller; perhaps flags the example.

clue.text: From watch, make oral statement about time

indicators.note: about means around, so the oral statement word encloses the time letter

parts.note: parol is a legal term for an oral declaration, as opposed to a written one

explanation.surface: From the watchtower, someone gives a spoken report about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: PAROL is a legal word for something said rather than written; 'From' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to keep watch over an area by moving about it, so watch and patrol are close synonyms.
